conviction_note: The findings sum to a mild negative (-1.9). The company's own documents show tight liquidity, with expensive bridge debt backed by the chairman's stock pledge and working capital down to $3.0M, plus a full turnover of CEO, CFO and COO before the first print under new management. Against that, revenue is tracking above a full-year guide that is easy to reach (H2 implied at $76-81M against $59M in Q2 alone). With no option chain, no usable reaction history and a Q3 bar that cannot be sourced, the uncertainty goes into p_up 45 and not into the size of the move: abs 13 on 98% realised vol in a $50k-a-day microcap.
bar: There is no sourceable Q3 consensus. Aggregators disagree on coverage (0 to 1 analyst), on the FY revenue forecast ($145.3M on TipRanks) and even on the report date (https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nxb/statistics). The bar used is the company's FY2026 revenue guide of $165-170M, raised in Q1 and maintained on 2026-08-13 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002067767/000149315226037764/ex99-1.htm). H1 revenue was $88.9M (10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2067767/000149315226037815/form10-q.htm), so H2 is implied at $76-81M, about $39M a quarter. print_vs_bar_pct is my Q3 estimate (~$41-45M) against that implied run-rate. Because no Q3 bar can be sourced, every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is 53.5K shares, 0.21% of float, 1.7 days to cover as of 2026-10-21 (https://equibles.com/stocks/nxb/summary), and 0.65-1.1 days through the summer (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/nxb/short-interest/). There is no crowded short and no squeeze mechanism. No option market exists (baseline options.status no_options_market), so there is no skew. The stock is a controlled company: Jason Ruegg holds ~53% (DEF 14C, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2067767/000149315226040849/formdef14c.htm), and 7.874M of his shares are pledged to the October lenders. The tape is 20-day run-up -26.1%, 5-day -2.9%, 64% below the 52-week high, 16% above the 52-week low, and roughly $49k a day of turnover (36k shares at $1.36).

findings.finding: Q3 liquidity was tight and refinanced at distress-like terms. Cash fell from $12.4M to $7.7M and working capital from $9.0M to $3.0M in H1 2026, and operating cash use was $18.1M in H1, mostly an $18.0M inventory build. In October the subsidiary took a $1.0M (up to $2.2M) 90-day bridge note at 15% plus a 2% fee. That note requires 100% of net equity from the sale of seven named boats to go to the lender, and is backed by the chairman's personal guaranty and a stock pledge with a $5.0M collateral top-up (default could transfer control). On 10-22 it drew $2.0M of a $5.0M revolver at 12.99%, secured by 7.874M pledged founder shares. The Q3 balance sheet in tonight's 10-Q will show how far cash and working capital fell. Asked what the money buys: pre-owned inventory and wholesale trades, partly corroborated by the H1 inventory build ($26.0M to $60.4M) and the record 255 units in Q2. But the 90-day maturity, the forced boat-sale prepayment and the founder margin-call collateral read as funding stress more than a ramp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None usable: the baseline has no prints on this entity (both prior prints belong to the predecessor Off The Hook YS) and the sweep marked history untrustworthy. The stock fell about 26% over the 20 sessions spanning these financing 8-Ks (10-13, 10-29), so some of this is likely in the price.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has fallen 26% in 20 days, which likely reflects part of this. What is not visible is the Q3 cash and working-capital number and whether the floor-plan lender (Red Oak, $60M line, $39.7M drawn at 6/30, where the 10-Q notes draws may exceed stated limits) tightened. If the market had fully priced a liquidity crunch, the tape would be near the 52-week low (it is 16% above it), and the chairman's pledge collateral ($5M at ~$1.36 means about 3.7M shares) would be the focus of commentary; I found none.
findings.independence: The revolver terms are in a different 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2067767/000149315226049199/form8-k.htm, 2026-10-29), and the H1 cash and working capital are in the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2067767/000149315226037815/form10-q.htm). The August convertible (10% OID, conversion price resetting to the lower closing bid every six months, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2067767/000149315226039033/form8-k.htm) points the same way. All are company filings and they share one theme.

findings.finding: Q3 is the first print under an almost entirely new top team: CEO Ross Tannenbaum from 2026-09-28 (predecessor Brian John stepped down), CFO Chad Corbin resigned 2026-10-05 with no successor named, and a new COO (ex-Fanatics) from 2026-11-06. The 10-29 release was titled 'sharpen focus on its core pre-owned boat business'. That raises the odds of a reset on the call: the FY $165-170M guide could be withdrawn or reframed, or the new-boat sales from the Apex acquisition de-emphasised, with one-off charges. The guide itself is easy to reach on revenue, so a cut is not forced by the numbers. The risk is a new CEO resetting profitability expectations, after H1 adjusted EBITDA of -$0.5M and Q2 net loss of $2.1M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No usable history on this entity. CEO compensation from FY2027 is tied to adjusted-EBITDA breakeven (8-K 2026-09-29), which suggests profitability, not revenue, is the line the new team will be judged on.
findings.why_not_priced: The changes are public, but nobody has said what the new team will do to the guide. There is no preview, no analyst note and no Q3 business update; the 10-29 release gave no operating metrics. If a reset were expected, the stock would already have broken its 52-week low, and the COO's options would not have been struck at $1.40 on 11-06, only about 3% above spot.
findings.independence: The CEO appointment and its EBITDA-linked pay are at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2067767/000149315226044890/form8-k.htm, the COO appointment at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2067767/000149315226051241/form8-k.htm, and the 'sharpen focus' framing at https://www.newswire.com/news/nextboat-secures-financing-to-support-growth-and-sharpen-focus-on-its-core-pre (2026-10-29). These are separate filings, but this is an inference from management turnover, not a document stating a guidance change.

findings.finding: Revenue should land at or above the guide-implied run-rate. H1 2026 revenue was $88.9M, so the maintained FY guide of $165-170M needs only $76-81M in H2, about $39M a quarter. Q2 alone was $59.1M (+88% YoY, a record 255 boats), with Apex Marine (acquired May) and Bellhart (May 22) in for only part of the quarter. Q3 2025 was $24.0M, about 23% below Q2 2025's $31.3M. Applying the same seasonal step-down to Q2 2026 gives about $45M for Q3, roughly +85% YoY and above the guide-implied ~$39M. This lands inside what the company has guided to.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No usable history on this entity. The record Q2 with +88% revenue (2026-08-13) was followed by a stock that kept falling, from about $2.1 in August to $1.36 now, so this name has not been paying for revenue growth.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregators carry a stale FY revenue forecast ($145.3M on TipRanks), below the company's own guide, so where a screen shows a bar it is low. But the market has not paid for revenue on this name since August, and the line the stock trades on now is cash and losses. If revenue were being priced, a company guiding to ~$167M at a ~$34M market cap would not sit near its lows.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 revenue of $24.0M is at https://quartr.com/events/nextboat-inc-nxb-q3-2025_FRs4cImr, and the H1 figure at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2067767/000149315226037815/form10-q.htm. MarineMax said on 2026-07-23 that late-model used boats were 'a pretty hot commodity' (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/marinemax-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-23/), a weak supporting proxy for pre-owned demand. The seasonal step-down is my inference from one prior year.

findings.finding: Industry read-across from MarineMax, NextBoat's strategic partner and the largest U.S. boat retailer, which reported its July-September quarter on 2026-11-04 (after NXB's last operating update): revenue $520.1M, down from $552.2M; same-store sales -5.7%; management cited a 'challenging retail environment'. MarineMax also agreed to be sold to Safe Harbor for $53/share, closing by end-2026. The NXB-MarineMax partnership (preferred wholesale and trade-in partner, a warrant for up to 1.25M shares, dealer portal in testing) can be ended by either side on 90 days' notice, so its future under a new owner is an open question for the call.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer print that landed after NextBoat last spoke, and nothing ties it to NXB in the wire. But it is mainly new-boat retail, where NXB is mostly pre-owned, and MarineMax's own comment on used boats was positive in July. That is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: The partnership terms and 90-day termination right are in the 10-Q subsequent-events note (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2067767/000149315226037815/form10-q.htm). The used-boat counterpoint is at https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/marinemax-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-23/. This is a proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: An S-1 filed 2026-08-28 for an underwritten primary offering of 3.4M new shares (plus 600k secondary and a 600k over-allotment, assumed price $5.00) is still on file with no withdrawal on EDGAR. At $1.36 the primary would raise only about $4.6M gross, and it would add about 14-16% to the 25.1M shares outstanding. On 10-29 the new CEO said debt was chosen over a common stock offering 'to limit dilution'. The print is the usual window to launch such a deal, but the CEO's stated preference makes a launch inside this window less likely.
findings.why_not_priced: The registration is public but has had no press coverage, and the deal was sized at a $5 assumption, so it has dropped out of view. If an offering were expected the stock would show heavier volume and weakness into the print. Volume is thin (36k a day) and the 5-day move is only -2.9%.
findings.independence: The CEO's debt-over-equity statement is at https://www.newswire.com/news/nextboat-secures-financing-to-support-growth-and-sharpen-focus-on-its-core-pre (2026-10-29). It cuts against a near-term launch and is the reason this is sized small. The EDGAR filing list (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0002067767.json) shows no RW.

findings.finding: Positioning leaves no squeeze fuel and no crowded long. Short interest is 0.21% of float (1.7 days to cover, 2026-10-21) and about 53% of shares sit with the chairman. The stock is down 26.1% over 20 sessions into the print, so the bar set by price has fallen with it.
findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning, not news. It is included so the panel sees the drawdown, which the core's free control (-run_up_20d) would read as a long. The drawdown has visible causes (the financing and management turnover above), so I give it little weight.
findings.independence: The run-up is from the sealed baseline tape. Short-interest history is at https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/nxb/short-interest/.

findings.finding: A related-party slip lease, signed before the board approved it and ratified afterwards: on 2026-11-04 the subsidiary signed a 7-year triple-net lease of 22 Wilmington slips ($8,950 a month, ~$823k over the term) from an LLC controlled by director Zebulon Hadley IV. That LLC had just bought the slips for $1.4M from entities of chairman and 53% holder Jason Ruegg. The board ratified it on 11-12. It is small in dollars, but it is one more governance item a new team brings to its first call, alongside a CFO vacancy.
findings.why_not_priced: It was filed on the Friday before the print, and I found no coverage of it.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. My mild negative agrees with the 26% 20-day drawdown, which already discounts part of the liquidity and management story, so I keep p_up near 50 (45) rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 4 (financing is a question): the money buys pre-owned inventory, partly corroborated by the H1 inventory build and record Q2 units, so the liquidity finding moved from -1.5 to -1.0 rather than being kept as pure distress.

Rule 6 (bar unsourced; finding inside the guide): with no Q3 consensus and revenue landing inside the company's own easy FY guide, the revenue finding moved from +1.0 to +0.5, and every finding is capped small.

Rule 5 (proxy and drawdown): the MarineMax read-across is new-boat-heavy and contradicted on used boats by MarineMax's own July comment, so it moved from -0.5 to -0.3. The positioning/drawdown finding moved from +0.5 to +0.2.

Rule 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the S-1 overhang finding's caveat (the CEO prefers debt to equity) moved it from -0.5 to -0.4. The management/guidance-reset inference moved from -1.0 to -0.8 because the guide is easy on revenue.
Rule 8 (thin coverage): abs_move_pct went from 12 to 13. p_up stays at 45.
